newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Sandoz to study Systemix decision.
newsitem.headline: Sandoz to study Systemix decision.

text.p: Swiss pharmaceuticals concern Sandoz AG said on Tuesday it was disappointed by a decision by independent directors of Systemix Inc to reject an unsolicited Sandoz bid but planned to study it before taking any further action.

Systemix, a Palo Alto, Calif., biotechnology company, said its independent directors rejected the unsolicited Sandoz offer of $17 per share for the outstanding Systemix shares that it did not already own.
Systemix said the decision was based in part on the advice of Lehman Brothers that the offer was inadequate and not fair to the minority shareholders from a financial point of view.
Systemix also said it remained willing to discuss an acquisition by Sandoz at an "appropriate" price.
Systemix specialises in the development of new therapies for major disorders of the blood system based on the use of human hematopoletic stem cells.
Collaboration between the two companies began in 1991 and in 1992 Sandoz acquired a 60 percent interest in Systemix.
The Swiss company increased this stake to 71.6 percent on a fully diluted basis in 1995.
